DUPLICATE of `mesodermic-vaporish-seaslug` (`0d15-59a4-e140-444b`) — closing.

That ticket is the compaction lane's own `discovered_from` bug for the same defect ("Sweep walks full git history per ticket under the store lock"), it is already `in_progress`, and its fix is Gerrit **1739**, in review now: one history walk per sweep hoisted OUTSIDE the lock, scoped staging, and a mid-run re-yield — which covers both halves of what I described (the per-event `git log --full-history` cost AND the stand-aside probe running only once, before the lock is taken).

I filed this independently after hitting it from an unrelated lane, without finding the existing ticket first. The concrete field evidence — 24+ minutes at 0.0% CPU, two blocked closes, a sweep spawned by a different worktree blocking this one, and the observed leading-wildcard pathspec command — has been carried over as a comment on seaslug, along with two suggestions that may sit outside 1739's scope (making the lock holder identify itself as optional housekeeping, and surfacing the "a skipped sweep is a no-op" guarantee somewhere a blocked operator would actually see it).

Nothing here needs to stay open. Linked `duplicates` seaslug.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom
Every `rebar transition ... closed` now detaches a compaction sweep (`rebar._commands.compact_trigger.run_sweep`, landed in `e0a55d5fac` / `d2dea317ec`). Observed today: a sweep held `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` for **24+ minutes**, during which every rebar write host-wide failed:

```
flock: could not acquire lock after 181s (holder: pid=57999 held=47s pid_state=live)
WARNING rebar._store.lock: write lock still held after 60s (pass 1/3) — retrying
```

It blocked a `set-file-impact`, then a `transition ... closed` (which aborted with `could not acquire lock` after its completion verification had already run). A second sweep — spawned by a DIFFERENT worktree's close (`ci-config-schema-gate`) — did the same a few minutes later, so this is host-wide and recurring, not one bad run.

## The sweep is not hung; it is quadratic-ish
The process sits at **0.0% CPU** because it is I/O-bound on git. It spawns one child at a time:

```
git -c log.showSignature=false -C <tracker> log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-renames \
    --format=%H -- '*<event-id>*.json'
```

That is a `--full-history` pathspec walk of the ENTIRE tracker history, with a LEADING-WILDCARD glob (so no pathspec fast path), run once PER EVENT. Cost scales as (events to fold) x (history length), and both grow with the store.

## Why this contradicts the feature's own design
`run_sweep`'s docstring is explicit that compaction "is optional housekeeping and must yield to work someone is waiting on, never compete with it", and that "a skipped sweep is a no-op for correctness (the events stay live and the next trigger folds them)".

The stand-aside probe (`_lock.write_lock_is_busy`) implements that — but it runs **ONCE, before** taking the store lock. After that the sweep holds the lock for its whole multi-minute run, so a writer arriving one second later waits the full duration. The guard prevents the sweep from STARTING during contention; nothing makes it yield to contention that arrives afterwards.

The design's own correctness argument is what makes the fix cheap: because an abandoned sweep is a no-op, the sweep is free to bail at any point.

## Suggested directions (not prescriptive)
- **Re-probe and yield mid-sweep**: check `write_lock_is_busy` between units and abort when a writer is waiting. Aligns with the stated contract and is correctness-free.
- **Do not hold the store lock across the whole sweep**: take it per fold, or fold into a scratch area and take it only to commit.
- **Fix the per-event git walk**: one `git log --diff-filter=A --format='%H' --name-only` pass building an id->commit index costs one history walk total instead of one per event.
- **Bound the work per trigger** so a large backlog drains over several sweeps rather than one long hold.

## Impact
Closes, `set-file-impact`, comments and reviews all block behind it, and the failure mode reads as a mysterious multi-minute hang rather than 'housekeeping is running'. In this session it required manually SIGTERMing sweeps twice to make progress — safe per the design's own no-op guarantee, but not something every operator will know.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A foreground store write arriving while a sweep is running acquires the lock within seconds rather than waiting for the sweep to finish; verified by a test that starts a sweep over a store with pending folds and asserts a concurrent write completes promptly.
- [ ] The sweep detects a waiting writer mid-run and stands down, leaving the store consistent and the unfolded events live (the documented no-op outcome).
- [ ] Event->commit resolution does not run one `git log --full-history` per event; verified by asserting the number of git invocations does not scale with the event count.
- [ ] A sweep interrupted at any point leaves no partial state that a later sweep cannot fold.
